paper_notes: The 4-4 star point remains most frequent.
desc_2007a: Hoshi 4-4 — sin cambio, sigue siendo el mas frecuente

paper_notes: Komoku (3-4) also remains as second most frequent pattern.
desc_2007a: Komoku 3-4 — sin cambio, sigue siendo el 2do mas frecuente

paper_notes: A low approach to a 3-4 point is nowadays more urgent than both a low approach to 4-4 (pattern 3a) and a high approach to a 3-4 (pattern 4a).
desc_2007a: Approach bajo a 4-4 hoshi (en 2025 sustituido por approach bajo a 3-4)

paper_notes: A san-san invasion is more urgent than a high approach to an opponent's komoku.
desc_2007a: Approach alto a komoku — superado por invasion san-san (mismo que 11b en 2025)

paper_notes: This standard sequence after a san-san invasion leaves the invader in gote, suggesting the invaded stone may reply with tennuki before extending.
desc_2007a: Invasion san-san a hoshi (2007: solo inicio, 2025: joseki completo de 5 jugadas)

paper_notes: Once white extends, it is less likely that black will tennuki, considering the result of pattern 5b.
A low approach to the 4-4 is now less frequent than a san-san invasion, see pattern 5a.
desc_2007a: Approach bajo a 4-4, keima oblicuo — permanece en rango 7, menos frecuente vs san-san

paper_notes: This approach resembles the joseki pattern in 6a but is actually a low approach to the opponent's enclosure from the 4-4 point. The fact that this enclosure pattern does not appear without the approach, suggests this move follows most of the time.
desc_2007a: Patron en rango 8 (2007) — 8b actual "se asemeja al joseki 6a"

paper_notes: A joseki continuation to pattern 5b, not as frequent.
desc_2007a: Joseki komoku+san-san (era rango 9 en 2007; descendio a rango 18 como 18b)

paper_notes: Two space jump from komoku appears as the most urgent form of enclosing a corner.
desc_2007a: Salto simple desde komoku (en era IA el salto doble 10b es preferido)

paper_notes: A high approach to komoku descends from 4th to 11th most frequent pattern.
desc_2007a: Patron desconocido en rango 11 del 2007 (approach alto era rango 4 como 4a)

paper_notes: Another continuation from pattern 5b precedes its subsequent joseki moves in patterns 14b, 15b and 17b.
This move is now less frequent, see pattern 7a.
desc_2007a: Approach bajo 5ta linea a 4-4 (ver patron 7a) — ahora menos frecuente

paper_notes: This joseki pattern naturally appears after a san-san invasion, but an extension from white's stone in the third line is not always the immediate follow-up, suggesting white's tennuki.
desc_2007a: Joseki san-san + extension (rango 14 en 2007, version menos desarrollada)

paper_notes: Though less frequent, this sequence from san-san invasion joseki also suggests white's tennuki, instead of following up with hane as in pattern 14b.
desc_2007a: Joseki san-san hane — rango 15 en 2007, menos frecuente que 14b

paper_notes: This pattern has become less frequent, see 8a.
desc_2007a: Approach a cercado alternativo (rango 16, ver patron 8a del 2007)

paper_notes: Similarly to pattern 14b, this sequence suggests black's tennuki immediately after white's hane.
desc_2007a: Hane+respuesta en joseki san-san — rango 17 en 2007

description: Joseki menos frecuente en juego moderno
paper_notes: This joseki pattern is less frequent in modern play, see 9a.
desc_2007a: Joseki komoku+san-san en rango 18 (era rango 9 como 9a, ahora menos frecuente)
